original_question: How can one study the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables by constructing the associated varieties through gluing familiar secant varieties and by using representation theory to describe their defining equations?
target_in_paper: The paper’s nearest official target is the concrete open problem on the slide 'Models with Hidden Variables': 'Consider the variety of 4×4×4-tables of tensor rank at most 4. Do the known polynomial invariants of degree five and nine suffice to cut out this variety?' This is also repeated in the Conclusion as the first of the three concrete open problems. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly captures the paper’s broad framing: it is about the geometry and commutative algebra of graphical models with hidden random variables, and it explicitly mentions approaching these models via secant-variety constructions and representation theory. That wording closely matches the paper’s 'General Problem' on page 1. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
missing_details: The paper does not ask this as a broad program about hidden-variable graphical models in general; it narrows immediately to one fixed concrete model, namely 4×4×4 tables of tensor rank at most 4. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
The ambient space is explicit: the model lives in C^4 ⊗ C^4 ⊗ C^4 with coordinates p_{ijk}, where i,j,k ∈ {A,C,G,T}. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The model is given parametrically by p_{ijk} = ρ_Aiσ_Ajθ_Ak + ρ_Ciσ_Cjθ_Ck + ρ_Giσ_Gjθ_Gk + ρ_Tiσ_Tjθ_Tk; your draft does not specify this parameterization. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The paper introduces the homogeneous prime ideal I of this model in the polynomial ring Q[pAAA, pAAC, pAAT, ..., pTTG, pTTT]; the question concerns this homogeneous ideal, not just a vague 'associated variety.' ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The paper explicitly identifies the same object under several equivalent descriptions: mixture of independent random variables, naive Bayes model, the CI model [X1 ⟂ X2 ⟂ X3 | Y], and the third secant variety of P^3 × P^3 × P^3. A stand-alone question should state at least one of these exact identifications. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The degree restrictions are essential: the open problem is specifically about the known homogeneous invariants in degrees 5 and 9, not an unrestricted representation-theoretic description of all defining equations. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The paper makes the known equations more precise via Proposition 1 and Proposition 2: a 1728-dimensional quintic GL(C^4)^3-module in degree 5, and an 8000-dimensional degree-9 GL(C^4)^3-module generated by the Strassen invariant. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

Homogeneity matters: the paper asks for homogeneous polynomial invariants and a homogeneous prime ideal. Your draft omits this projective/homogeneous formulation. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

There is no asymptotic parameter, no 'for all sufficiently large m' clause, and no nilpotency condition here; the problem is finite, fixed, and specific to the 4×4×4 rank-≤4 model. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))

The phrase 'suffice to cut out this variety' should be preserved, because that is the paper’s wording; if one wants extra precision, it should be tied to determining the homogeneous prime ideal I rather than replacing the paper’s question by a broader one. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be the variety of 4×4×4 tables (p_{ijk}) with i,j,k ∈ {A,C,G,T}, given parametrically by p_{ijk} = ρ_Aiσ_Ajθ_Ak + ρ_Ciσ_Cjθ_Ck + ρ_Giσ_Gjθ_Gk + ρ_Tiσ_Tjθ_Tk, and let I = I(X) be its homogeneous prime ideal in Q[pAAA, pAAC, pAAT, ..., pTTG, pTTT]. Equivalently, X is the naive Bayes model / CI model [X1 ⟂ X2 ⟂ X3 | Y], i.e. the third secant variety of P^3 × P^3 × P^3. Determine I; in particular, do the known homogeneous polynomial invariants of degrees 5 and 9—namely the quintics of Proposition 1 and the degree-9 module generated by the Strassen invariant in Proposition 2—suffice to cut out X? ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: for the third secant variety of the Segre variety P^3 × P^3 × P^3, determine whether the known degree-5 and degree-9 homogeneous invariants described in Proposition 1 and Proposition 2 suffice to cut out the variety. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
justification: The draft is faithful to the paper’s broad motivation but not to its actual sharply posed open problem. The paper’s hidden-variable section begins with a general programmatic sentence very close to your wording, but it immediately specializes that program to one concrete question about the 4×4×4 rank-≤4 model. The next slides define the model parametrically, introduce its homogeneous prime ideal I over Q, identify the same variety with the naive Bayes / CI / secant-variety model, and then isolate the relevant degree-5 and degree-9 modules in Propositions 1 and 2. For that reason, the refined question should be about this single specific model and these exact degrees, not about hidden-variable graphical models in general. ([math.berkeley.edu](https://math.berkeley.edu/~bernd/imaprob.pdf))
